clue.text: Noisy accompaniment for a reel

parts.note: a reel sounds like a dance or fishing gear, but here it is a reel of film, and the noisy accompaniment is the recorded music and dialogue that runs alongside the pictures

explanation.walkthrough: A 'reel' suggests a Scottish dance needing a fiddler, but think of a cinema reel: the audio strip running beside the pictures.
explanation.definitionFit: The recorded audio of a film, music and speech, runs on a strip beside the images of each cinema reel.

clue.text: Tolerable repeat of sound broadcast

indicators.note: the sound is given twice over
the word for broadcast is said aloud

parts.note: to sow seed is to broadcast it by scattering

explanation.surface: Radio programmes repeated are bearable enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' is not radio: it means scattering seed, SOW, which sounds like SO; 'repeat of' doubles it.
explanation.definitionFit: Middling, only passable, neither good nor bad.

clue.text: Open mid-June festivity

indicators.note: the middle letters of the month name are taken

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: A summer party begins in the middle of the month.
explanation.definitionFit: To unfasten or unwrap something is to open it.

clue.text: Dreadfully sad once I lost?

indicators.note: the following words are dreadfully muddled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is terribly unhappy now that they have been beaten.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the anagram and the definition: someone miserable after losing.
explanation.definitionFit: Inconsolably unhappy, as a loser may be.

clue.text: Extra condition for competitor in race

definitions.meaning: a clause added to a contract or bill
a jockey or cyclist in a race

explanation.definitionFit: An added clause to a document, and a jockey or cyclist taking part in a race.

clue.text: Associate in business left a long way below

indicators.note: in a down clue the later pieces sit below the word for business

parts.note: Co is short for company
a league is an old measure of about three miles

explanation.surface: A business partner leaves the firm far behind.
explanation.definitionFit: A fellow worker or partner in one's job.

clue.text: Cursing the odds in England

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters of the word England, first, third, fifth and seventh, are picked out

explanation.surface: Someone notes how much swearing the gamblers do over the odds in England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the odds in' picks the 1st, 3rd, 5th and 7th letters of England. 'Odds' looks like betting talk.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned mild oath, the sort of thing said when cursing.

clue.text: New song with drum, with an expert aiming for perfect pitch

indicators.note: the letters are made new by rearranging them

explanation.surface: A musician with absolute pitch writes a new song with drums.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perfect pitch' suggests music, but it is a sports pitch, like a cricket square.
explanation.definitionFit: The person who tends a cricket or football field aims to keep the playing surface immaculate.

clue.text: Express disapproval about one lower in value

indicators.note: the word for disapproval goes about, around, the letter for one

parts.note: to deprecate is to express disapproval
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone disapproves of a person who is held in low esteem.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose or reduce worth, as a car does over time.

clue.text: How female retains seat, as parties become confused

parts.note: the parties in a dispute or match are its sides
to addle is to grow muddled

explanation.surface: A woman keeps her place in the assembly while the political groups fall into disarray.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'seat' is a seat on horseback, not in parliament: women once rode with both legs on one side of the saddle.
explanation.definitionFit: The traditional riding position for a woman, both legs on one side, is how she kept her seat on horseback.

clue.text: Brilliant stroke from all-rounder in sporting contest

indicators.note: the round letter is placed in the middle of the word for the contest

parts.note: a cup is a sporting competition, as in the FA Cup
O is a round letter, so 'all-rounder' gives it

explanation.surface: A cricketer who bats and bowls produces a fine shot in a cup match.
explanation.walkthrough: An 'all-rounder' is a cricketer who both bats and bowls; here it is just the letter O, which is round all over.
explanation.definitionFit: A master stroke or sudden successful move, a triumph pulled off at a stroke.

clue.text: Dame selecting actors for variety entertainment

parts.note: broad is slang for a woman, as is dame
casting is choosing actors for roles

explanation.surface: A theatrical dame chooses actors for a variety show.
explanation.walkthrough: BROAD is American slang for a woman, as is 'dame'.
explanation.definitionFit: Radio and television transmission brings a variety of entertainment to the public.

clue.text: This event could make road ace fortune

definitions.text: This event could make road ace fortune

parts.words: This event could make road ace fortune
parts.note: the event is a famous long cycle race whose winner, a star of road racing, can make a fortune; the words look like anagram fodder but the letters do not fit

explanation.walkthrough: 'road ace fortune' looks like an anagram, but it has two letters too many; it is a cryptic description of a race that enriches a cycling star.
explanation.definitionFit: France's great annual multi-stage cycle race, whose winner becomes rich and famous.

clue.text: Exultant celebration from scene of investment, we hear

indicators.note: the place name is spoken aloud

parts.note: Mafeking was besieged (invested) in the Boer War, 1899-1900

explanation.surface: Bankers celebrate wildly over the place where the money was invested.
explanation.walkthrough: 'investment' is siege, not finance: Mafeking in South Africa was besieged, and London's wild celebration at its relief gave this word.
explanation.definitionFit: The riotous street rejoicing in London when Mafeking was relieved gave its name to any extravagant public jubilation.

clue.text: Jointly divided, so to speak? Clearly

definitions.meaning: to speak clearly, enunciating each word

explanation.definitionFit: Segmented with joints, like an insect's limb, and to express oneself with clarity in speech.

clue.text: Constable's work is so striking

definitions.meaning: a police constable's job includes taking people into custody; the painter Constable is a false lead

explanation.walkthrough: Constable suggests the painter John Constable and his works, but it is a police constable.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking suspects into custody is a policeman's job, and a remarkable, eye-catching thing is also described this way.

clue.text: Mutual activity reformulating party line

indicators.note: the words are reformulated, their letters put in a new order

explanation.surface: A political group is redrafting its official policy together.
explanation.definitionFit: Reciprocal action and influence between two parties.

clue.text: Musician's very inconclusive attack

indicators.note: something without a conclusion lacks its ending, so the last letter goes

parts.note: to assail is to attack

explanation.surface: A player's assault on the piece is strong but never quite finishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inconclusive' removes the final L of ASSAIL. 'Musician's very' means the word for 'very' in a musical direction, as in allegro assai.
explanation.definitionFit: In Italian tempo markings this word means extremely, as in allegro assai for very fast.

clue.text: Ruff with king found in pack

indicators.note: the king's letter is found inside the word for pack

parts.note: to pack a space is to fill it
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: In a card game, a ruff is played with the king turning up in the deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruff' and 'king' and 'pack' suggest trumping at cards, but a ruff is also a pleated collar.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruff is an Elizabethan pleated collar, an ornamental gathered edging.

clue.text: Cutting tax rate, initially, with delight

indicators.note: the opening letters of the words tax and rate are taken

parts.note: to enchant is to delight

explanation.surface: A government is pleased to announce it is reducing the rate of tax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutting' seems to go with 'tax rate', but it is the definition: sharp, incisive.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharply incisive remarks are biting; cutting criticism has an edge.

clue.text: Aggressive response in bar, with swearing

parts.note: a counter is a bar in a shop or pub
'blast!' is an oath, so swearing gives it

explanation.surface: Someone at a pub replies angrily with a stream of oaths.
explanation.definitionFit: A vigorous retort, an attack mounted in reply to criticism.

clue.text: Lead for boxer in role as heavyweight

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the words role as heavyweight

explanation.surface: A fighter is cast as a heavyweight in a film.
explanation.walkthrough: The boxer is a dog, not a fighter.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog's lead, such as a boxer wears on a walk.

clue.text: Wake up in jail

definitions.meaning: to rouse or begin to move

explanation.definitionFit: To rouse oneself from sleep, and slang for a prison.

clue.text: Obligation we're under, apparently

parts.note: an obligation is something that rests ..., and read as two words the burden is literally placed on top of us

explanation.walkthrough: Split into two words the answer says the burden rests on top of us, so we are under it.
explanation.definitionFit: A burden of responsibility or duty.

clue.text: Russian ruler I spotted leading front line

indicators.note: the letter I goes in front, ahead of the word for front line

parts.note: the van, short for vanguard, is the leading part of an army

explanation.surface: A tsar sees his troops advancing at the head of the attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spotted' is a link: I is seen leading VAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Several tsars bore this name, notably the Terrible, the first crowned tsar of Russia.

clue.text: Like a host subjected to bloodthirsty attack

definitions.text: Like a host subjected to bloodthirsty attack

parts.words: Like a host subjected to bloodthirsty attack
parts.note: the host is not an army but an animal carrying parasites, and the bloodthirsty attackers are tiny jumping insects that feed on it

explanation.walkthrough: 'host' suggests an army or a party host; it is the animal on which parasites feed.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog bitten by its parasites is in a sorry, shabby state, the word also meaning squalid.

clue.text: Dark horse among political leaders

definitions.meaning: a horse of a pale colour is called by this colour name
Earl ... was a British Prime Minister (1830-34)

explanation.walkthrough: 'Dark horse' reads as one phrase but splits into three definitions; Earl Grey was a 19th-century British Prime Minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Gloomy overcast weather, a whitish horse, and Earl Grey the Prime Minister of the Reform Act all share this word.

clue.text: Change to graph, say, for mathematician

indicators.note: the letters are to be altered into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone suggests altering the chart for the numbers expert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' looks like a link meaning 'for example', but it is part of the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek geometer of the famous theorem on right-angled triangles was a mathematician.
